summary_html: **Educators/school staff** observing indicators of abuse/neglect report to CPS under state mandatory-reporter lists built on the federal CAPTA floor.

key_cases.case_name: Berry v. Watchtower Bible & Tract Society of New York, Inc.
key_cases.holding: Affirming dismissal, the court held that even assuming congregation elders were obligated to report suspected abuse under RSA 169-C:29, the abused children had no private cause of action for the failure to report and the religious organizations owed them no common law or fiduciary duty of protection.
key_cases.relevance: For institutions that supervise children, the case separates the statutory reporting mandate from the special-relationship and premises-based duties that can support tort liability.
key_cases.quote: the plaintiffs may not bring a private cause of action for the alleged failure of the elders to comply with RSA 169-C:29

key_cases.holding: The court held that a post-secondary institution owes its students a fiduciary duty to provide an environment free of sexual harassment by faculty, affirmed the jury verdict for the student on that claim together with enhanced compensatory damages and prejudgment interest, and remanded the Title IX issues.
key_cases.relevance: Where the reporting statute supplies no private remedy, this is the New Hampshire authority imposing an independent institutional duty on a school toward a student sexually abused by staff, and it is the fiduciary standard Berry v. Watchtower applies.
key_cases.quote: In the context of sexual harassment by faculty members, the relationship between a post-secondary institution and its students is a fiduciary one.

state_agency.name: Division for Children, Youth and Families
state_agency.hotline: 1-800-894-5533 (in-state only) or 603-271-6562; DCYF Central Intake is staffed 24 hours a day, including weekends and holidays

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 169-C:29
Physicians, surgeons, county medical examiners, psychiatrists, residents, interns
Registered nurses and hospital personnel (admission, examination, care and treatment)
Teachers, school officials, school nurses, school counselors
Social workers, day care workers, and any other child or foster care workers
reporting_details: New Hampshire is a universal-reporter state: RSA 169-C:29 lists physicians, dentists, psychologists, registered nurses and hospital personnel, teachers, school officials and school nurses, social workers, day care and other child or foster care workers, law enforcement officials and clergy, and closes with “any other person having reason to suspect that a child has been abused or neglected,” all of whom “shall report the same in accordance with this chapter.” RSA 169-C:30 sets the route and the form: an oral report “shall be made immediately by telephone or otherwise, and followed within 48 hours by a report in writing, if so requested, to the department” — the Department of Health and Human Services, which takes reports through the DCYF Central Intake Unit at 603-271-6562 or 1-800-894-5533 (in-state only), staffed 24 hours a day including weekends and holidays.
